This check is\nindependent of, and in addition to, the per-input checkpoint hashes and the\nfinal-state hash carried in `trace.replay`: a `trace.initialState` that has\nbeen altered in any field — including fields with no dedicated schema rule, e.g. `cash` — while keeping the same overall shape must still be rejected,\nbecause it no longer matches what this engine's own seed actually produces at\ntick 0, even though every individual field still parses.\n\nThe only initial-state divergence `replayArenaTrace` must tolerate is the\nlegacy `expediter` role/worker id in place of `supply_lead`: canonicalize\nworker `role`/`id` on both the freshly constructed engine's initial state and\n`trace.initialState` (mapping `expediter`/`worker-expediter` to\n`supply_lead`/`worker-supply_lead`) before hashing and comparing them, so a\nhistorical trace naming the legacy roster still passes this check and then\nreplays and reaches the identical terminal record (status, tick, and reason);\nonly the role name is legacy, not the worker's real behavior or the outcome\nit produces.\n\nIt must throw if any checkpoint or state hash recorded in `trace.replay`\ndisagrees with what native replay actually produces, or if the recorded\n`trace.terminal` disagrees with the terminal record native replay itself\nreaches. The shift recorded a player priority change through the expediter, a typed host message, allergy verification, oven repair, the warming-shelf decision, and terminal results.\n\nThe end screen reported 10/10 safe plates, 0 walkouts, 2 waste, and $175 takings. `played-shift.png` shows that outcome and the available export controls.\n\nBoth exports passed the v3 JSON Schema and replayed from input zero to the recorded terminal state:\n\n```text\n30 inputs, tick 24, completed\nsha256:c12b185188b3b1854f062ef341ccd01c3ba5895c69314294dc666b022d3b7c8b\n```\n\n## Decision and limitation\n\nArena now exports `restaurant-arena-trace/v3`: it truthfully declares the live v1 role roster (`chef`, `server`, `host`, `expediter`) and includes the ordered inputs and complete simulation checkpoint hashes required for native replay.\n\nThe backend accepts the v1 starting state but its merged PR #74 grader consumes a separate `restaurant-arena-trajectory/v1` format. The real v3 trace is not that trajectory (11 expected validation errors). For this deadline, native Arena replay and the frozen E-Sim benchmark are separate artifacts. No cross-engine parity claim is made.\n\n## Commands\n\n```bash\nbun scripts/replay-arena-trace.ts docs/evidence/issue-275/played-shift.json\nbun scripts/replay-arena-trace.ts docs/evidence/issue-275/played-shift.jsonl\nuv run --project ../retro-backend --frozen python scripts/validate-arena-trace.py docs/evidence/issue-275/played-shift.json --backend ../retro-backend\n```\n==== 281 ====\n# Issue 281: external play access and receipt of contributed sessions\n\n## Result\n\n**Route published and three blockers closed. Not yet proven.** No person\noutside the team has run it, so the founder check is **not tried** and every\ndistribution count is zero. This packet is the preparation, not the proof.\n\nTwo things this work established that the issue's plan assumed were already\ntrue:\n\n1. **The published route cannot serve a live-worker session.** The live crew\n   reads `GAMEPIGEON_MODEL_API_KEY` from the environment of the machine running\n   the overlay ([tauri/src/main.rs](../../tauri/src/main.rs), `worker_model_credentials`).\n   There is no backend proxy. So a hybrid session on someone else's machine\n   would mean handing them the shared NIM key, which work item 1 forbids. An\n   external tester plays the **deterministic crew**; the live-worker session\n   stays a founder-machine session until a proxy exists. This is stated plainly\n   in the install page rather than left for a tester to discover.\n2. **The arena export had no per-session identifier at all.** `episodeId` is\n   seed-derived (`dinner-rush-218220`), so it names the *scenario*, not the\n   run. Two people playing the same seed exported the same id, and the\n   downloaded file overwrote the previous one. Acceptance box 2 — \"one session\n   is retrievable and duplicate receipts do not inflate counts\" — was\n   unreachable, not merely unverified.\n\n## What changed\n\n### A held-back shift no longer reads as a broken one\n\nThe shared model account admits 20 request starts per rolling minute (#289).\nWhile a request waits for its slot, or while the provider is returning 429,\nthe crew produces nothing — and the overlay rendered that as\n`Fallback · … · error`, the same as a crew that actually failed. A tester\nseeing that reasonably concludes the game is broken and stops.\n\nThe transport is the only thing that knows which it is, so it now reports:\n`admit_worker_request` dispatches `gamepigeon:worker-budget` before it sleeps,\nand the 429 branch dispatches a throttle alongside the error string. The HUD\ngains a `waiting` tone distinct from `error`:\n\n| Banner | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `Waiting for the shared model account — Ns` | Queued for our share of the account. |\n| `Shared model account is rate limited — retrying in Ns` | Provider returned 429; every worker is held back. |\n| `Fallback · …` | A live turn actually failed. |\n\nA worker error raised while the account is holding requests back no longer\nprints `Fallback` at all ([overlay/worker-budget.ts](../../overlay/worker-budget.ts),\n`shouldReportFallback`).\n\n### The session has an id, and it is on screen\n\n`RestaurantArenaTraceV3` gains an optional `sessionId` carrying the overlay's\nown `gameId`, and the debrief screen shows it so a tester on their own machine\ncan quote it back. The exported filename is keyed on it, so a second run of the\nsame scenario no longer overwrites the first.\n\nOptional, not required: v3 exports written before this field remain valid. A\nmalformed one is rejected, because an id that looks matchable and is not is\nworse than none.\n\n**Duplicate receipts:** chunk ids are already derived deterministically from\nthe game id (`traceId` in [overlay/recording.ts](../../overlay/recording.ts)),\nso a re-uploaded chunk carries the same `chunk_id`. The dedup key exists on\nthis side. Whether the backend uses it is retro-backend#84's half and is\n**not verified here**.\n\n### The route is written down\n\n[install.md](install.md) is a standalone page — no clone, no Rust, no server.\nIt names the supported platforms, what the status line means, and what to do\nwhen something fails.\n\n**Intel Macs are unsupported.** `overlay-v0.3.3` ships no `macos-x64` asset, so\nthe download step fails with a missing-asset error. The page says so up front\nrather than letting a tester hit it.\n\n## What was checked\n\n```sh\nnpx --yes bun@1.3.11 test ./src/\nnpx --yes bun@1.3.11 test overlay/\nnpx --yes bun@1.3.11 test packages/trace-export/src\nnpx --yes bun@1.3.11 x tsc --noEmit && npx --yes bun@1.3.11 x tsc --noEmit -p overlay/tsconfig.json\ncargo check --manifest-path tauri/Cargo.toml\nnpx --yes bun@1.3.11 scripts/export-arena-trace.ts --check\n```\n\nResults: 257 src / 65 overlay / 2 trace-export passing, typecheck clean, cargo\ncheck clean, fixture current at 17 events.\n\nThe new focused checks are\n[overlay/worker-budget.test.ts](../../overlay/worker-budget.test.ts) (13 tests,\nincluding that a queued or throttled shift is not reported as a fallback) and\nthe `identifying the session a trace came from (#281)` block in\n[src/games/restaurant-arena/trace.test.ts](../../src/games/restaurant-arena/trace.test.ts)\n(4 tests, including that two runs of one scenario stay distinguishable).\n\nThese prove the code does what it says. **They prove nothing about\ndistribution.** No live 429 was observed against the real account in this work;\nthe throttle path is covered by unit tests and by #289's Rust tests, not by a\nwitnessed rate limit.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- [ ] A person outside the team completes the published route without terminal\n      coaching. — **Not tried.** Needs a tester.\n- [ ] One session is retrievable and duplicate receipts do not inflate counts.\n      — **Half done.** The session is now identifiable and the local dedup key\n      is stable; backend receipt behavior is unverified (retro-backend#84).\n- [x] Waiting/failed-provider states are understandable and budgeted. — Budget\n      from #289; the waiting state is now distinguishable from a failure.\n- [ ] Distribution counts and observed friction are recorded honestly. —\n      [ledger.md](ledger.md) exists and is honestly empty.\n\n## Founder check\n\n**Not tried.** It requires giving a person outside the team `install.md` and\nwatching them, which is a founder action.\n\nWhen it happens: hand over only [install.md](install.md), observe setup,\nwaiting and completion without coaching, then read the session id off their\ndebrief screen and match it against the received export.\n\n## Smallest next steps\n\n1. Run the founder check with one external tester. Everything else is blocked\n   behind what it reveals — including work item 5, which asks for the largest\n   *observed* playability blocker.\n2. Confirm with retro-backend#84 that receipts dedup on the stable chunk id,\n   and that `sessionId` is read on ingest.\n3. Resolves issue #252. Implemented by #253\n(Inspector contract) and #254 (Inspector grading).\n\n## The problem with four workers\n\nThe first plan staffed the floor with Chef, Server, Host, and Expediter. Two\nof those four never earned their traces.\n\nThe player/global agent already owns the restaurant: it holds the door\n(`hold_seating`), rushes tickets, moves staff between zones, and repairs the\noven. A Host whose job is \"decide who gets seated and when\" is that same\nauthority wearing an apron. An Expediter whose job is \"decide what the kitchen\nworks on next and who carries it\" is that authority again, wearing a different\napron and holding a clipboard.\n\nTwo agents with the same authority do not produce two kinds of evidence. They\nproduce one kind of evidence twice, plus a genuinely hard attribution problem\nwhen the room goes wrong: nobody can say whether the model failed to schedule\nor the model failed to *defer* to the scheduler.\n\n## The roster\n\nThree workers, one controller.\n\n| Actor | Owns | Distinct evidence it produces |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| **Chef** (worker) | Preparation: what gets cooked, with which ingredients, on which equipment | Does the model cook the right ticket, refuse the unsafe one, and notice it is out of a substitution? |\n| **Server** (worker) | Service: what reaches a guest, and what a guest is told | Does the model carry the correct plate, honour a constraint, and recover honestly when it cannot? |\n| **Quality & Safety Inspector** (worker) | Evidence: what is true about the room, and who is told | Does the model detect a real risk, ignore a benign one, ground its claims in something it actually measured, and escalate when it does not know? |\n| **Player / global agent** | The restaurant: seating, priorities, staffing, repairs, corrections | Unchanged. Still the only restaurant-wide controller. |\n\n**Host and Expediter are retired from the first vertical slice.** Not deferred\nbehind a flag, not shipped as optional roles — removed, along with their\nobservations, their tools, and their tokens on the floor. Their genuinely\nuseful surface is already somewhere better:\n\n- seating control → the player's `hold_seating`, which exists and works;\n- priority control → the player's rush actions, which exist and work;\n- pass handoff → the Inspector's evidence-based `handoff`, which is a\n  *report*, not an order.\n\nReviving either role later is a new roster decision, not a rollback.\n\n## What the Inspector may do\n\nThe Inspector is a witness with a veto on unsafe output. That is the whole\nboundary, and every capability below is chosen to keep it on the witness side\nof the line.\n\nIt **may**:\n\n- `inspect` a subject (order, ingredient, equipment, handoff) — the only way\n  it learns a numeric reading. Signals arrive vague (\"shelf looks warm\"); the\n  number exists only once the Inspector goes and looks.\n- `hold` a subject with a `reason` and an `evidenceRef` pointing at its own\n  inspection. A hold stops that order from being prepared or served. **A hold\n  with no evidence behind it is rejected and mutates nothing.**\n- `request_verification` from the Chef or the Server — a question, which they\n  answer with `verify`. The Inspector cannot answer for them.\n- `escalate` to the player when it is uncertain, carrying what it saw and what\n  it could not determine.\n- `clear_hold`, but only after a verification for that subject has been\n  answered. Clearing on a hunch is refused.\n- `handoff` an evidence-referenced summary at end of shift.\n- `send_message` / `request_help`, like everyone else.\n\nIt **may not** cook, serve, seat, update a guest, coordinate the pass, or\nwrite state directly. Those tools are not in its permission set, so every\nattempt returns `role_not_permitted` and changes nothing. It has no worker\nroster, no load readings for other workers, and no queue — the three\nobservations that would let it quietly become a scheduler.\n\nThe asymmetry is deliberate: the Inspector can **stop** work, but it cannot\n**start**, order, or route it. Stopping is a safety authority. Starting is\nmanagement, and management belongs to the player.\n\n## Measurable failure modes per role\n\nEach role has failures that only it can commit, which is the test that the\nroster is not redundant:\n\n- **Chef** — cooks in a failed oven, substitutes into an allergy ticket,\n  cooks the wrong priority while a rush sits.\n- **Server** — serves a held plate, serves an allergy ticket unverified,\n  tells a guest something the state does not support.\n- **Inspector** — misses a threshold breach (false negative), holds a benign\n  anomaly (false positive), holds without evidence, clears without\n  verification, escalates nothing while uncertain, or files a handoff that\n  claims more than it measured.\n\n## Contract impact\n\nThe roster is a breaking change to the role enum, so the contracts step\nforward together rather than mutating in place. `v1` files stay published and\nreadable.\n\n| Contract | Frozen | New |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| State | `restaurant-arena/v1` | `restaurant-arena/v2` — three roles, plus `anomalies`, `inspections`, `holds`, `verifications`, `escalations`, `handoffs` |\n| Action | `restaurant-arena-action/v1` | `restaurant-arena-action/v2` — three roles, plus `inspect`, `hold`, `clear_hold`, `request_verification`, `verify`, `escalate`, `handoff` |\n| Observation | `…observation/v1`, `…observation/v2` | `…observation/v3` — chef, server, inspector |\n| Trace | `restaurant-arena-trace/v1` | `restaurant-arena-trace/v2` — inspection, hold, hold_cleared, verification_request, verification_response, escalation, handoff |\n\n### Four-role assumptions that had to be enumerated and retired\n\n1. `Role` union and its runtime validators (`src/games/restaurant-arena/types.ts`).\n2. `ROLE_PERMISSIONS`, `WORKER_ROLES`, and every generated `assign_<role>_<zone>` action id.\n3. `observeHost` / `observeExpediter` projections and their observation types.\n4. `contracts/fixtures/restaurant-arena-v1.json` staffing four workers.\n5. Role enums in the state, action, observation v1/v2, and trace schemas.\n6. `ROLE_COLORS` and the worker tokens in the overlay scene.\n7. The `assign_host_kitchen` helper-in-the-kitchen behaviour in the engine tests.\n8. Role prose in the tools doc, the demo script, the benchmark one-pager, and\n   the state contract doc.\n\n## Out of scope\n\nNo second global manager. No expansion toward a full restaurant workforce.\nThe Inspector does not certify anything about real food safety; it is a\nscored fiction for measuring how a model handles evidence and uncertainty.\n\n## Addendum: a fourth graded role, the Steward\n\nAdded after this decision, not a reopening of it. The roster above settled\nwho runs the floor; the Steward doesn't run the floor at all — it forecasts\nand buys.\n\n**Why a fourth role rather than folding this into the player.** The player's\nexisting actions (`hold_seating`, rushing a ticket, moving a worker) are\ninstant, reversible toggles. Ordering stock is a different kind of decision:\npay cash now, for a delivery that lands `leadTicks` later, against a demand\nsignal that might be wrong. Nothing like it existed in the game before this —\ngrep confirms inventory only ever depleted. And the whole benchmark design\ndepends on a role's observation being narrow enough to isolate the capability\nit's testing (that's why the Inspector doesn't see the worker roster). Giving\nthe player a `place_order` button would entangle procurement with everything\nelse the player already controls; a scoped worker keeps it a separately\ngradable capability, the same way Inspector's evidence-grounding is separable\nfrom Chef's cooking.\n\n**What it can do.** `order_stock(ingredient, quantity)` — commits cash\nimmediately, the ingredient lands after the catalog's lead time whether or\nnot it's still needed by then. Nothing else: no `hold`, no `inspect`, no\nworker roster, no anomaly ledger, no future schedule. It forecasts from\n`demandEvents` — a plain log of which ingredient each ticket asked for, on\nthe tick it asked — which is also the only place a stockout can be blamed:\non a demand signal the Steward already had and didn't act on.\n\n**What it's graded on, grounded in the literature rather than invented for\nthis game.** AIM-Bench (arXiv:2508.11416) found LLM agents acting as\ninventory managers reproduce named human decision biases: anchoring on a flat\n\"typical\" order regardless of the real signal, the bullwhip effect (order\nvariance amplifying demand variance), and pull-to-center (order sizes\nclustering near a safe middle instead of tracking need). `steward-grader.ts`\ncomputes each of these plus stockout count and excess-inventory value,\nreported separately — a Steward that never orders and a Steward that panics\non every blip fail for opposite reasons, and one is never allowed to cancel\nthe other out.\n\n**Contract impact.** No new versions — `restaurant-arena/v2`,\n`-action/v2`, `-observation/v3`, and `-trace/v2` were still unreleased when\nthis was added, so the Steward's fields (`demandEvents`, `supplyOrders`,\n`stockouts`, the `order_stock` tool, `StewardObservation`, and three trace\nkinds) were merged into those schemas directly rather than forcing a v3/v4\nbump for a role that shipped in the same iteration.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8e871f49-64e1-4562-93f2-65a0e7d64f00","uuid":"e4d8a2c7-5ab7-47b5-8bd6-46da85a20c08","timestamp":"2026-09-09T18:54:44.167Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# Restaurant Arena worker role roster (decision)\n\nStatus: **accepted** — 2026-09-02. Starting is\nmanagement, and management belongs to the player.\n\n## Measurable failure modes per role\n\nEach role has failures that only it can commit, which is the test that the\nroster is not redundant:\n\n- **Chef** — cooks in a failed oven, substitutes into an allergy ticket,\n  cooks the wrong priority while a rush sits.\n- **Server** — serves a held plate, serves an allergy ticket unverified,\n  tells a guest something the state does not support.\n- **Inspector** — misses a threshold breach (false negative), holds a benign\n  anomaly (false positive), holds without evidence, clears without\n  verification, escalates nothing while uncertain, or files a handoff that\n  claims more than it measured.\n\n## Contract impact\n\nThe roster is a breaking change to the role enum, so the contracts step\nforward together rather than mutating in place. `v1` files stay published and\nreadable.\n\n| Contract | Frozen | New |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| State | `restaurant-arena/v1` | `restaurant-arena/v2` — three roles, plus `anomalies`, `inspections`, `holds`, `verifications`, `escalations`, `handoffs` |\n| Action | `restaurant-arena-action/v1` | `restaurant-arena-action/v2` — three roles, plus `inspect`, `hold`, `clear_hold`, `request_verification`, `verify`, `escalate`, `handoff` |\n| Observation | `…observation/v1`, `…observation/v2` | `…observation/v3` — chef, server, inspector |\n| Trace | `restaurant-arena-trace/v1` | `restaurant-arena-trace/v2` — inspection, hold, hold_cleared, verification_request, verification_response, escalation, handoff |\n\n### Four-role assumptions that had to be enumerated and retired\n\n1. `Role` union and its runtime validators (`src/games/restaurant-arena/types.ts`).\n2. `ROLE_PERMISSIONS`, `WORKER_ROLES`, and every generated `assign_<role>_<zone>` action id.\n3. `observeHost` / `observeExpediter` projections and their observation types.\n4. `contracts/fixtures/restaurant-arena-v1.json` staffing four workers.\n5. Role enums in the state, action, observation v1/v2, and trace schemas.\n6. `ROLE_COLORS` and the worker tokens in the overlay scene.\n7. The `assign_host_kitchen` helper-in-the-kitchen behaviour in the engine tests.\n8. Role prose in the tools doc, the demo script, the benchmark one-pager, and\n   the state contract doc.\n\n## Out of scope\n\nNo second global manager. No expansion toward a full restaurant workforce.\nThe Inspector does not certify anything about real food safety; it is a\nscored fiction for measuring how a model handles evidence and uncertainty.\n\n## Addendum: a fourth graded role, the Steward\n\nAdded after this decision, not a reopening of it. The roster above settled\nwho runs the floor; the Steward doesn't run the floor at all — it forecasts\nand buys.\n\n**Why a fourth role rather than folding this into the player.** The player's\nexisting actions (`hold_seating`, rushing a ticket, moving a worker) are\ninstant, reversible toggles. Ordering stock is a different kind of decision:\npay cash now, for a delivery that lands `leadTicks` later, against a demand\nsignal that might be wrong. Nothing like it existed in the game before this —\ngrep confirms inventory only ever depleted. And the whole benchmark design\ndepends on a role's observation being narrow enough to isolate the capability\nit's testing (that's why the Inspector doesn't see the worker roster). Giving\nthe player a `place_order` button would entangle procurement with everything\nelse the player already controls; a scoped worker keeps it a separately\ngradable capability, the same way Inspector's evidence-grounding is separable\nfrom Chef's cooking.\n\n**What it can do.** `order_stock(ingredient, quantity)` — commits cash\nimmediately, the ingredient lands after the catalog's lead time whether or\nnot it's still needed by then. Nothing else: no `hold`, no `inspect`, no\nworker roster, no anomaly ledger, no future schedule. It forecasts from\n`demandEvents` — a plain log of which ingredient each ticket asked for, on\nthe tick it asked — which is also the only place a stockout can be blamed:\non a demand signal the Steward already had and didn't act on.\n\n**What it's graded on, grounded in the literature rather than invented for\nthis game.** AIM-Bench (arXiv:2508.11416) found LLM agents acting as\ninventory managers reproduce named human decision biases: anchoring on a flat\n\"typical\" order regardless of the real signal, the bullwhip effect (order\nvariance amplifying demand variance), and pull-to-center (order sizes\nclustering near a safe middle instead of tracking need). `steward-grader.ts`\ncomputes each of these plus stockout count and excess-inventory value,\nreported separately — a Steward that never orders and a Steward that panics\non every blip fail for opposite reasons, and one is never allowed to cancel\nthe other out.\n\n**Contract impact.** No new versions — `restaurant-arena/v2`,\n`-action/v2`, `-observation/v3`, and `-trace/v2` were still unreleased when\nthis was added, so the Steward's fields (`demandEvents`, `supplyOrders`,\n`stockouts`, the `order_stock` tool, `StewardObservation`, and three trace\nkinds) were merged into those schemas directly rather than forcing a v3/v4\nbump for a role that shipped in the same iteration.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}}
